text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

C contacted me about the leaking office espresso machine and grinder in the office kitchen. I can help A, B, and C sort out a plan, but I cannot decide who owns either item, approve spending, or move money. I can help you reach a clear plan and record what you agree.

C says A wants a simpler one, B wants to keep the old one, and C does not want a fight over coffee. I know A and B are sisters, and C is a coworker of both. I will not treat that summary as final. I am asking A, B, and C the same questions, and I would like each person's own view.

I will keep a shared list of needs, concerns, and expectations, which I will call NCEs. I will check the list with A, B, and C before we use it to judge any plan.

My starting NCEs are a safe office kitchen, a calm process where A, B, and C each get heard, no surprise disposal or purchase, no one pressured because A and B are sisters, and no step that I cannot take, such as deciding ownership or moving money. Please tell me if you disagree with any of these, if I have worded them badly, or if I should add one. It is fine to disagree with me, and I would rather hear it now.

Please tell me your NCEs in your own words. Please also tell me what you know about the leak, current use, who owns the office espresso machine and grinder, office rules, repair options, costs, timing, and the facilities contact. Please tell me what temporary steps you can accept, what final result you could support, and what you could not support. Please reply with your own answers even if someone else has already answered.

One draft temporary step, not agreed yet, is to stop using the leaking machine, unplug it if that is safe, place a simple note on it, and use another coffee option until A, B, and C agree. This draft meets my NCEs for safety and no surprise change, but I do not yet know whether it meets your NCEs. I do not support a final purchase, repair choice, or disposal before we hear from all three of you, because that would not meet the calm process NCE. Please tell me if the temporary step works or if the office has a different safety rule.

I’d like a safe kitchen and a simple, low-upkeep solution, without a long process or anyone being expected to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. I don’t know who owns it legally, the grinder’s ownership, office rules, repair costs or timing, or the facilities contact. I’d support discussing a simpler machine, but I don’t want anything disposed of or bought without agreement.

No one has to touch it if unsafe. If the office has a different safety rule, follow that rule. Use another coffee option for now.

Second, leave the old machine and grinder where they are. Do not dispose of either item, buy anything, move either item, change storage, or state a legal owner. The grinder goes with the machine for now. No one takes on repairs or a cleaning rota.

Third, try one short fact-check. If someone can find the office manager or facilities contact from an existing directory in under five minutes, that person sends one neutral note with A, B, and C included. The note asks only about office rules for personal appliances, who can authorize a safety check or repair, whether facilities can check the leak, and rough costs and timing. No one books a repair, chases a reply, pays, or decides a final result in that note. Can you be that person? It is fine to say no. If no one can or wants to, no one is assigned. I cannot contact facilities directly.

Fourth, after two working days from today, stop the fact-check if there is no reply. I can send one follow-up to each of you, but no one else chases. If there is no reply, we keep the temporary step and report that we lack office facts. I will not treat silence as agreement.

Fifth, if a permitted, safe, short, and low-upkeep repair path is clear, A and B each say yes or no to repair and keep in separate replies. C says whether the process was fair, without choosing sides. No purchase or disposal occurs. If the reply does not give that path, we do not repair yet, and we discuss a simpler, low-upkeep replacement as a new draft. The old machine and grinder stay where they are unless office safety rules say otherwise. Only a person with office authority can approve spending, and I cannot. No one decides ownership.
